content.comment_body: I'm trying to prevent the operator from changing the display screens on the [product_name] Operator Device. Specifically, I want the arrow keys to have no effect, so accidental access to clock or monitoring screens is blocked. I haven't found an option to do this yet. Best regards [user_name]

Hello [user_name], This question has come up before; you might want to review earlier threads about disabling the device buttons. One participant suggested a workaround, though it might be somewhat unconventional. Currently, there is no programming feature to block screen changes when cursor, ESC, or OK buttons are pressed. Even with a [product_name] module paired with the new text display, those buttons will access various menu, navigation, status, and clock screens. If you physically disable the buttons as suggested by others, you can keep a specific message displayed using the Message Text with the En input, possibly inverting it if desired. Avoid setting up other message texts and set the message priority to the highest value (since 0 is the lowest priority and lower-priority messages can override it). Apologies, that's the only solution I can provide.

That approach isn't ideal. Using the navigation keys, it's too easy for someone to stop the process, which really shouldn't be possible. Are there any alternative suggestions? Best regards [user_name]

I agree—when the product is used as an HMI, it's vulnerable to users experimenting by pressing buttons. It would be helpful if [company_name] introduced enhanced security features for the Operator Device, since it currently allows navigation with the cursor, ESC, and OK buttons. While I consider the product cost-effective and high quality, there's always room for improvement, especially with a software or firmware update. I'm interested to see what changes come with the next hardware release, as previous versions had impressive advancements. Hopefully, [company_name] will continue incorporating user feedback.
Hello to everyone exploring the function buttons! Take a look at my post on 'How to disable the buttons'. [url] Cheers

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing ways to restrict navigation controls on [product_name] Operator Devices to prevent operators from accessing unintended screens or halting processes. Existing configurations do not allow full customization or locking of navigation buttons, which exposes these devices to unintentional or unauthorized changes and affects operational security.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for options to limit or disable navigation and function keys on [product_name] Operator Devices to boost process security and prevent accidental interference by operators.
